text_simplified: A daughter needs to feel paternal care, tenderness, and emotional attention, so parents must not become so preoccupied that their children feel neglected despite their parents' presence. We have a noble example in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whenever he saw his daughter Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her), he welcomed her and said: "Welcome, my daughter," and seated her to his right or to his left (Sahih Muslim 2450); and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon his daughter 'A'ishah while she was ill, kissed her cheek, and said: "How are you, O my little daughter?" (Sahih al-Bukhari 3918).

review_defects.why: The English title omits 'رحمة النبي ﷺ ببناته' (the Prophet's mercy to his daughters), making the example generic.
The Arabic simile 'like orphans despite the presence of their parents' is paraphrased down to 'feel neglected,' dropping the evocative imagery.
